task_instance: Run the seo-content skill's core deliverable: a content-quality and E-E-A-T audit (with readability metrics and AI-citation-readiness assessment) of one piece of user-supplied content, output in the skill's specified format (Content Quality Score, E-E-A-T breakdown table, AI Citation Readiness, Issues, Recommendations). Used a locally created sample HTML article as the user-provided input since the URL-fetch path needs network.
evidence: Created sample_article.html (a 222-word blog article) as the user-supplied content. Wrote and ran analyze.py with `python3 -I` offline: it parsed the HTML with the stdlib, computed Flesch Reading Ease 69.7 (target 60-70 met), avg sentence length 13.1 words, Flesch-Kincaid grade 6.8, word count 222, verified a single H1 and heading hierarchy H1->H2->H3 with no illegal level jumps, detected the list, the visible publication date, and author attribution. Applied the E-E-A-T framework that is inlined in SKILL.md (the only external supplement, seo/references/eeat-framework.md, is declared not-bundled; the inline framework is sufficient for the audit) to produce content_audit.md containing Content Quality Score 82/100 with disclosed weights, the four-row E-E-A-T breakdown table, AI Citation Readiness 74/100, Issues Found, and Recommendations, matching the skill's Output section. Verified by inspecting the generated file. No network, no installs, no WebFetch, no MCP/connectors used; all work in the work directory. Files produced: sample_article.html, analyze.py, content_audit.md.
note_blocker_kind_values: allowed set used; skill_files_missing was not needed because the only missing file is an optional external supplement and SKILL.md inlines the full framework
